newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sydney Casino shares fall on Packer report.
newsitem.headline: Sydney Casino shares fall on Packer report.

text.p: Shares in Sydney Harbour Casino Holdings Ltd fell nearly three percent in early trade on a newspaper report that media tycoon Kerry Packer might withdraw from his intention to buy the casino's management contract.
At 10.4r a.m. (004r GMT), Sydney Casino shares were six cents or 2.75 percent down at A$2.12 with 1.2 million shares traded.
Shares in Packer's media group Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd (PBL) were up 14 cents to A$6.85 on low volume.
PBL has an option to buy 85 percent of the Sydney casino management contract from U.S. casino group Showboat Inc.

The Ausralian newspaper reported on Wednesday that PBL is expected to announce that it has decided not to take up the option to buy 10 percent of Sydney Harbour Casino from Showboat and management control of the casino, in order to focus on a planned bid for John Fairfax Holdings Ltd.
The Australian reported the option was believed to expire in the next fortnight. PBL announced in January it intended on spend over A$350 million on gaining control of the casino.
"The negative press report on PBL withdrawing from the casino is the only thing I can think of that is pulling the stock down," one Sydney-based casino analyst said.
"The Packer family has previously had a strong desire to buy the casino asset, but what their strategy is for the future, I can't say," the analyst said.
A Packer-led consortium lost the bidding for the 12 year Sydney casino monopoly licence to the Showboat-Leighton Holdings Ltd consortium.
Packer challenged this decision all the way to the high court, which earlier this month dismissed the appeal.
Packer's PBL has a 15 percent stake in Fairfax, which is tipped to be a takeover target if the government eases the current media ownership rules.
The government is currently reviewing media ownership policy.
